answer: Reputation-Weighted Escrow Release. Each identity locks a lotus escrow that only unlocks after counterparties confirm completed work, so value accrues to identities with real transaction history rather than fresh clones. A new identity must forge that history by completing genuine jobs before it can transact at scale. Attackers pay the full escrow plus the labor cost of building a crystal-clear record per clone, making mass cloning costlier than operating one honest identity.
